[00:00] Interviewer: Okay, it's recording. Can you hear me all right, Noah?
[00:04] Noah: Yes, yes, I can hear you fine.
[00:07] Interviewer: Let's start with your birthdays. What do you remember?
[00:11] Noah: Every birthday, my mother made seaweed soup. Miyeokguk. She said it was what her mother made for her in Korea, so you never forget who fed you. Even the year we had almost nothing, there was seaweed soup on the table in the morning.
[00:38] Interviewer: Did she cook other things from Korea?
[00:42] Noah: Kimchi soup, all winter. She made it in the big red pot, and the whole stairwell smelled of it. The neighbours complained at first, and then they started knocking to ask for a bowl.
[01:05] Interviewer: Tell me about school.
[01:09] Noah: I was the new boy in fourth grade, and I didn't know anyone. My friend Sarah sat next to me on the first day, because nobody else would. She talked the whole time, mostly about her brother Tom, who was older and already worked at the shipyard. I only ever knew him from her stories.
[01:41] Interviewer: Are you still in touch with her?
[01:44] Noah: Sarah, yes. She still sends me a card every Christmas.
[01:58] Interviewer: What about summers?
[02:01] Noah: Two summers we went back to Busan, my mother and me, to stay with my uncle Jae-won. He had a fishing boat, and he let me hold the wheel when we came into the harbour.
